messages:
maria: Storm + short fuse. Power went out at the house so I dragged the folding desk into the garage, hooked a tiny car battery UPS to an old 4G router and a camping lantern. jury-rigged ethernet from the trunk. photos in thread.
jamal: Garage pop-up office? legendary. pics pls :camera_with_flash: 
mar ia: here — https://files.slack.com/files-pri/T12345-F67890/garage-office.jpg (terrible lighting, the lantern is doing what it can)
sophie: Not gonna lie this is peak suburban startup energy. how's internet latency over the car hotspot?
maria: ~120ms to east coast, stable-ish. download 8–10 Mbps, upload 3 Mbps. it's enough for calls and quick testing.
ravi: If you need lower latency, can you run a tiny local nginx reverse proxy so the VPN handshake happens from your laptop locally? (won't help throughput but may reduce connection setup pain)
maria: oh nice — did `ssh -D 1080 -C user@jumpbox` and routed browser through socks, felt smoother.
leo: neighbor drone literally hovered over the garage to check out the light and knocked a zip tie. chaos. :grimacing: (reacted :laughing: by jamal)
maria: zip tie fixed, taped the lantern to a cinder block. engineering solutions. :hammer_and_wrench:
infra-bot: Reminder: please avoid connecting personal routers to corporate networks. If you need exfil for work, ping infra for a temporary approved config.
sophie: also vote: should we start a WFH emergency kit doc? "car-battery + mesh + lantern" deserves a page. thumbs up/down
jamal: thumbs up from me :thumbsup:
maria: will add a quick how-to with photos later. lesson: you can do remote work from a garage but bring duct tape, zip ties, and patience.
leo: 10/10 content for random. more garage office pics pls.
mar ia: uploading one more from inside the trunk… https://files.slack.com/files-pri/T12345-F67891/trunk-router.jpg
